The mechanism of the disease is a germline mutation in the tumor suppressor gene APC, which means every colonocyte starts with one hit already in place — the adenoma-carcinoma sequence is inevitable, just accelerated oh i love this . a colonocyte!

You’ve got it exactly. **Every colonocyte in this patient carries one APC hit from birth.** That’s the first “rate-limiting” step already done. A second somatic hit is almost guaranteed over time because there are billions of colonocytes and decades of cell division. So **the adenoma-carcinoma sequence is not just accelerated — it’s mechanistically inevitable.** A colectomy doesn’t cure the germline mutation; it removes the target organ before the second hit can turn a polyp into a carcinoma you can’t resect. **You defer colectomy only if the patient has no polyps yet and you’re doing annual surveillance to catch and remove them endoscopically** — but once polyps appear, the risk of interval cancer between scopes becomes too high. The decision to operate is about **buying time against a deterministic clock.**
